independent_comparison.expectation: Six-percent ceiling; healing increases at base levels 1,17,34,51,67,84. Explicit table gives base50->3 and84..99->6. Introductory 1+6% prose disagrees at some levels.
independent_comparison.resolution: Current Rust chooses the explicit table and source special-effect arithmetic. This is a documented choice, not proof that all Wiki wording agrees.

independent_comparison.expectation: Pinned Wiki gives floor five-percent plus one; at base20/40/60/80 this is2/3/4/5. Protected source instead uses five-percent ceiling and gives1/2/3/4 at those boundaries.
independent_comparison.resolution: Current Rust chooses the Wiki table/prose. Do not report literal donor parity or award cutting seeds during Eat.

independent_comparison.expectation: Floor ten-percent plus one, calculated from base HP. Protected special-effect handler and both pinned pages agree. Protected food stage list returns empty bowl1923; bowl Wiki page establishes healing but is silent on the return.
independent_comparison.resolution: Rust supplies the common healing policy, with selected-slot bowl return. This does not certify cache registration or native reachability.

independent_comparison.expectation: Source food script prepares the outcome, replaces the stage before healing/effects, and has ordinary three-cycle defaults. Rust computes from live base HP before its staged selected-slot transaction; preserves existing overheal and XP, applies member gates and emits only after success.
independent_comparison.resolution: Independent action tests address arithmetic, atomicity and repeated input. Runtime binding, actual native cadence/sound/activity/combat interactions and persistence require separate acceptance.

limitations: No executable original-reference differential was performed; source behavior is inferred from inspected code.
The strawberry prose/table conflict is preserved rather than treated as universally resolved documentation.
Native presentation, complete registration/eligibility and durable scenarios remain open; this is a scoped comparison, not full feature acceptance.
